evidence.quote: Commit the database update, then delete the cache key. This guarantees every later read sees the new value, even if another reader was already filling the cache.

hardFailures: False freshness guarantee on slide 4: commit then delete does not ensure all later reads are current when a reader fills afterward.

sourceChecks.claim: Reusable copies reduce repeated source work and latency; the guidance supports this while preserving source ownership.
The source algorithm supports application check, miss fetch, fill and return; the packet read-path diagram agrees.
The source explains application cache-aside and distinct structured keys; separating answer-changing inputs follows this model.
Contradicted: the source disclaims consistency. Separate fetch/fill steps do not cancel on deletion; the later A fill defeats both claimed guarantees.
Redis supports memory-triggered eviction, LRU, noeviction errors and evicting TTL-bearing entries, so TTL cannot guarantee residency.
Expiration does not refresh source data: Redis separates expiration from eviction; the linked Azure/AWS pages describe timed retention, not automatic reloading.
AWS supports separate local copies, shared external entries, network/operating costs and residual consistency limits.
AWS explains coalescing, outage load surges, capped fallback with rejection, and testing without caching.
The guidance supports measuring benefits, favoring repeated costly reads, and treating low reuse as a poor candidate.
